mil5.2.3:0.4: 3. Question on Fearing and Not Fearing Death
mil5.2.3:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this too was said by the Blessed One:
mil5.2.3:1.2: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’ And he also said:
mil5.2.3:1.3: ‘The arahant has gone beyond all fear.’
mil5.2.3:1.4: Does the arahant, Venerable Nāgasena, tremble from fear of punishment? And do beings in hell, blazing, boiling, scorched and thoroughly burned, fear death as they pass away from that great hell with its flaming masses of fire?
mil5.2.3:1.5: If, Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said
mil5.2.3:1.6: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death,’ then the statement ‘The arahant has gone beyond all fear’ is false.
mil5.2.3:1.8: ‘The arahant has gone beyond all fear,’ then the statement ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death’ is also false.
mil5.2.3:1.9: This two-horned dilemma has now come to you, and it must be resolved by you.”
mil5.2.3:2.1: “Your majesty, the Blessed One did not speak those words with reference to arahants:
mil5.2.3:2.2: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:2.3: The arahant is set apart from that case; for the arahant the cause of fear has been uprooted.
mil5.2.3:2.4: It was , your majesty, with reference to beings who still have defilements, who have an excessive view of self, and who are elated or dejected concerning pleasure and pain, that the Blessed One said:
mil5.2.3:2.5: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:2.6: For the arahant, your majesty, every destination is cut off, every womb is destroyed, rebirth-linking is struck down, the supporting beams of the house are broken, every dwelling-place in existence is uprooted, all formations are cut off, wholesome and unwholesome kamma are destroyed, ignorance is shattered, consciousness has been made seedless, all defilements are burned, the worldly conditions are transcended. Therefore the arahant does not tremble at any fears.
mil5.2.3:3.1: Suppose, your majesty, a king had four chief ministers, protectors who had won his trust and favour, and he had placed them in positions of great authority.
mil5.2.3:3.2: Then, when some business arose, the king commanded everyone in his realm: ‘Let all of you pay me tribute; and you four chief ministers, carry out that business.’
mil5.2.3:3.3: Would those four chief ministers, your majesty, feel dread from fear of the tribute?”
mil5.2.3:3.6: “Because the king placed them in the highest position, venerable sir. They owe no tribute; they have gone beyond tribute. The king’s command, ‘Let all pay me tribute,’ was made with reference to the rest.”
mil5.2.3:3.7: “In the same way, your majesty, the Blessed One did not speak those words with reference to arahants. The arahant is set apart from that case; for the arahant the cause of fear has been uprooted. It was with reference to beings who still have defilements, who have an excessive view of self, and who are elated or dejected in pleasure and pain, that the Blessed One said:
mil5.2.3:3.8: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:3.9: Therefore the arahant does not tremble at any fears.”
mil5.2.3:4.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, that statement does not leave anything out; ‘all’ is a statement without exception.
mil5.2.3:4.2: Give me a further reason to establish it.”
mil5.2.3:5.1: “Suppose, your majesty, the headman of a village commanded his messenger: ‘Come, messenger, quickly gather before me all the villagers in the village.’
mil5.2.3:5.2: The messenger, saying ‘Yes, master,’ would stand in the middle of the village and call out three times: ‘All villagers in the village, assemble quickly before the master!’
mil5.2.3:5.3: Then the villagers, at the messenger’s word, would hurry and gather, and report to the headman: ‘All the villagers have assembled, master; do what you need to do.’
mil5.2.3:5.4: So, your majesty, in gathering the householder men, the headman commanded all the villagers, yet not all of those commanded assembled; only the householder men did. And the headman accepted this, thinking, ‘These are all my villagers.’ The many others who did not come (women and men, slaves and servants, hired hands and workers, sick villagers, cattle, buffalo, goats, sheep, and dogs) were all left uncounted, because the command ‘Let all assemble’ had been given with reference to the householder men alone.
mil5.2.3:5.5: In the same way, your majesty, the Blessed One did not speak those words with reference to arahants. The arahant is set apart from that case; for the arahant the cause of fear has been uprooted. It was with reference to beings who still have defilements, who have an excessive view of self, and who are elated or dejected in pleasure and pain, that the Blessed One said:
mil5.2.3:5.6: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:5.7: Therefore the arahant does not tremble at any fears.
mil5.2.3:6.1: There is, your majesty, a statement with exceptions whose meaning has exceptions; a statement with exceptions whose meaning has none; a statement without exceptions whose meaning has exceptions; and a statement without exceptions whose meaning has none.
mil5.2.3:6.2: The meaning must be accepted in each case accordingly.
mil5.2.3:7.1: The meaning, your majesty, should be established by five means: by the direct text, by the essence, by the teacher’s lineage, by one’s own understanding, and by the superiority of reasoning.
mil5.2.3:7.2: Here the direct text means the suttas;
mil5.2.3:7.3: the essence means conformity with the suttas;
mil5.2.3:7.4: the teacher’s lineage means the teachers’ doctrine;
mil5.2.3:7.6: and superiority of reasoning means the reasoning that agrees with these four.
mil5.2.3:7.7: By these five means, your majesty, the meaning should be established.
mil5.2.3:7.8: Thus this question is well resolved.”
mil5.2.3:8.1: “Very well, Venerable Nāgasena; I accept it so.
mil5.2.3:8.2: Let the arahant be set apart in that case, and let the remaining beings tremble. But the beings in hell, experiencing painful, sharp, bitter feelings, with every limb and part of the body ablaze, their mouths wailing, lamenting, weeping and crying out, overwhelmed by unbearable agony, without protection, without refuge, with no one to turn to, drowned in sorrow, at their last and final destination, wholly given over to grief, amid the heat and fierce, harsh, scorching blaze, with great terrifying cries that breed dread, entangled in the sixfold garland of woven flames, their blazing flames spreading for a hundred leagues in every direction, in that wretched, burning great hell: do these, as they pass away, fear death?”
mil5.2.3:9.1: “But Venerable Nāgasena, is not hell wholly a place of painful feeling? Why then do those beings in hell, whose experience is wholly painful, fear death as they pass away from hell? Do they delight in hell?”
mil5.2.3:9.2: “Those beings in hell, your majesty, do not delight in hell; they long to be freed from it.
mil5.2.3:9.3: It is the very power of death, your majesty, that produces their dread.”
mil5.2.3:9.4: “Venerable Nāgasena, I do not believe this: that those who long for release should feel dread at passing away. That is a laughable thing, Venerable Nāgasena, that they should obtain what they long for and yet fear it. Convince me with a reason.”
mil5.2.3:10.1: “Death, your majesty, is a thing that frightens those who have not seen the truths; people tremble and are alarmed at it.
mil5.2.3:10.2: Whoever fears a black snake, your majesty, fears it because he fears death.
mil5.2.3:10.4: a lion... a tiger... a leopard... a bear... a hyena... a buffalo... a wild ox... fire... water... a stump... a thorn fears it because he fears death.
mil5.2.3:10.5: And whoever fears a spear fears it because he fears death.
mil5.2.3:10.6: It is death’s own intrinsic nature and power, your majesty; by this intrinsic power, beings with defilements tremble and fear death. Even beings in hell, your majesty, who long for release, tremble and fear death.
mil5.2.3:11.1: Suppose, your majesty, a fatty lump arose on a man’s body.
mil5.2.3:11.2: Afflicted by that disease and wanting to be rid of the trouble, he would summon a surgeon.
mil5.2.3:11.3: The surgeon, accepting his request, would prepare the instruments to remove the disease: he would sharpen a knife, heat a pair of iron probes in the fire, and have caustic salt ground on a grinding stone. Would that sick man, your majesty, feel fear at the cutting with the sharp knife, the burning with the heated probes, and the application of the caustic salt?”
mil5.2.3:11.5: “So, your majesty, even though that sick man longs to be free of the disease, dread arises in him from fear of the pain.
mil5.2.3:11.6: In just the same way, your majesty, even beings in hell who long for release from hell feel dread from fear of death.
mil5.2.3:12.1: Suppose, your majesty, a man had offended a lord, been bound with chains and thrown into a dungeon, and longed to be freed. The lord, wishing to release him, summoned him.
mil5.2.3:12.2: Would that man, your majesty, knowing ‘I am guilty,’ feel dread at seeing the lord?”
mil5.2.3:12.4: “So, your majesty, even though that man who offended the lord longs for release, dread arises in him from fear of the lord.
mil5.2.3:12.5: In just the same way, your majesty, even beings in hell who long for release feel dread from fear of death.”
mil5.2.3:13.1: “Give me yet another reason, venerable sir, by which I may be satisfied.”
mil5.2.3:13.2: “Suppose, your majesty, a man had been bitten by a venomous viper, and from the effect of the venom he fell down, rose, rolled and thrashed about. Then another man, using a powerful spell, brought that very viper that had bitten him and made it suck back the venom. Would that poisoned man, your majesty, feel dread as the snake that had bitten him approached, even though it came to save him?”
mil5.2.3:13.4: “So, your majesty, even when such a snake approaches for his safety, dread arises in him.
mil5.2.3:13.5: In just the same way, even beings in hell who long for release feel dread from fear of death.
mil5.2.3:13.6: Death, your majesty, is unwelcome to all beings; therefore beings in hell, though longing to be released from hell, fear death.”
mil5.2.3:13.7: “Well said, Venerable Nāgasena. It is so, and I accept it.”
